stem: A client has primary hyperparathyroidism. Which laboratory finding should the nurse expect?
rationale: NIDDK explains that in primary hyperparathyroidism one or more parathyroid glands are overactive and produce too much parathyroid hormone (PTH). Excess PTH raises blood calcium, so elevated blood calcium is the expected finding. C and D describe physiology opposite to primary hyperparathyroidism, and blood glucose is not the defining laboratory effect of excess PTH.
educational_objective: Associate primary hyperparathyroidism with excessive PTH production and elevated blood calcium.
source_organization: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK), National Institutes of Health
source_locator: Sections 'What is primary hyperparathyroidism?' and 'What do the parathyroid glands do?': overactive parathyroid gland(s) make too much PTH; too much PTH causes blood calcium to rise
source_claim_supported: Primary hyperparathyroidism causes excessive PTH production, and excess PTH raises blood calcium levels.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
